# peabiru

Travel-time matrices, accessibility, isochrones and detailed itineraries
by walking, cycling, driving and public transport, with fares, slope
costs and scenarios, on networks built from an OpenStreetMap extract,
GTFS public transport feeds and an optional elevation raster. It is a
Rust port of Conveyal’s [R5](https://github.com/conveyal/r5) routing
engine. The routing engine is written in Rust and runs inside the R
session: no Java is needed, and the network is built once, in memory,
and reused by every call. The same engine is behind the Python and
JavaScript packages and the command-line tool of the same name.

> **Authorship.** peabiru is an independent project. Its routing model
> is that of Conveyal’s [R5](https://github.com/conveyal/r5), and its
> fare calculator and parts of its trip planner are translated from
> [r5r](https://github.com/ipea/r5r) (Ipea); both are MIT-licensed, and
> their notices are kept in `LICENSE-THIRD-PARTY`. peabiru is not
> affiliated with or endorsed by Conveyal, Ipea or the r5r team. The
> port was written with the assistance of AI coding tools.

Website: <https://strategicprojects.github.io/peabiru-routing/> (this
package’s documentation is at
<https://strategicprojects.github.io/peabiru-routing/r/>).

[![Four maps of central Recife, one per mode, with the areas reached
from Praça do Derby within 15, 30 and 45 minutes walking, cycling,
driving and by public
transport.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/StrategicProjects/peabiru-routing/main/site/assets/figures/isochrones-rmr.svg)](https://strategicprojects.github.io/peabiru-routing/r/articles/recife-metropolitan.html)

| Function | What it computes |
|----|----|
| [`build_network()`](reference/build_network.md) | a network from one `.pbf`, any number of GTFS feeds and an optional elevation raster (`.tif`) |
| [`travel_time_matrix()`](reference/travel_time_matrix.md) | travel times by `"WALK"`, `"BICYCLE"`, `"CAR"` or public transport (`"TRANSIT"` or any of its modes, reached by walking, bicycle or car), with percentiles over a departure window |
| [`accessibility()`](reference/accessibility.md) | opportunities reachable from each origin, with five decay functions |
| [`expanded_travel_time_matrix()`](reference/expanded_travel_time_matrix.md) | the trip of every departure minute, with its breakdown |
| [`arrival_travel_time_matrix()`](reference/arrival_travel_time_matrix.md) | the latest trip that arrives by a given time |
| [`isochrone()`](reference/isochrone.md) | the areas or street segments reached within each cutoff |
| [`detailed_itineraries()`](reference/detailed_itineraries.md) | the legs of each trip, with their lines (the fastest trip, or the alternatives) |
| [`setup_fare_structure()`](reference/setup_fare_structure.md), [`read_fare_structure()`](reference/read_fare_structure.md), [`write_fare_structure()`](reference/write_fare_structure.md) | fare structures, which the routing functions take as `fare_structure` |
| [`pareto_frontier()`](reference/pareto_frontier.md) | the trade-off between travel time and fare |
| [`find_snap()`](reference/find_snap.md), [`street_network_bbox()`](reference/street_network_bbox.md), [`street_network_to_sf()`](reference/street_network_to_sf.md), [`transit_network_to_sf()`](reference/transit_network_to_sf.md) | where points snap, and the street and transit networks as `sf` |
| [`check_transit_availability()`](reference/check_transit_availability.md), [`get_gtfs_errors()`](reference/get_gtfs_errors.md) | the dates with service, and the errors in the GTFS feeds |

The routing functions also take scenarios of car speeds
(`new_carspeeds`, `carspeed_scale`) and of traffic stress for cyclists
(`new_lts`). What peabiru does not support stops with an error that says
so, for instance a fare structure that names a fare calculator (a
`type`) instead of fare rules; nothing is silently ignored.

## Installation

From GitHub, with [Rust](https://rustup.rs) installed (`cargo` and
`rustc` 1.81 or later):

\
`# install.packages("pak")`\
`pak``::`[`pak`](https://pak.r-lib.org/reference/pak.html)`(``"StrategicProjects/peabiru-routing@r-package"``)`\
\
`# or, with remotes`\
`# install.packages("remotes")`\
`remotes``::`[`install_github`](https://remotes.r-lib.org/reference/install_github.html)`(``"StrategicProjects/peabiru-routing@r-package"``)`

The branch `r-package` holds the released package with the sources of
the routing engine, so nothing else is downloaded while it compiles
(about a minute). The development version is in the directory `r/` of
the branch `main`: clone the repository and run `R CMD INSTALL r`.

## Example

\
[`library`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/library.html)`(`[`peabiru`](https://strategicprojects.github.io/peabiru-routing/r/)`)`\
\
`data_path`` ``<-`` `[`system.file`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/system.file.html)`(``"extdata/spo"``, package ``=`` ``"peabiru"``)`\
`network`` ``<-`` `[`build_network`](reference/build_network.md)`(``data_path``)`\
`points`` ``<-`` `[`read.csv`](https://rdrr.io/r/utils/read.table.html)`(`[`file.path`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/file.path.html)`(``data_path``, ``"spo_points.csv"``)``)`\
\
`ttm`` ``<-`` `[`travel_time_matrix`](reference/travel_time_matrix.md)`(`\
`  ``network``, ``points``, ``points``,`\
`  mode ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``"WALK"``, ``"TRANSIT"``)``,`\
`  departure_datetime ``=`` `[`as.POSIXct`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/as.POSIXlt.html)`(``"2019-05-13 14:00:00"``, tz ``=`` ``"America/Sao_Paulo"``)``,`\
`  percentiles ``=`` `[`c`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/c.html)`(``25``, ``50``, ``75``)``,`\
`  seed ``=`` ``42`\
`)`

## Class of the results

The functions return tibbles by default (`sf` tibbles for the results
with a geometry). `options(peabiru.output = "data.frame")` gives base
data frames and `options(peabiru.output = "data.table")` `data.table`s;
the rows, columns and values are the same whatever the class. There is
also a [comparison with
r5r](https://strategicprojects.github.io/peabiru-routing/r/articles/coming-from-r5r.html).

## Documentation

The package website is built from this directory with pkgdown, together
with the rest of the project’s documentation: run `site/build.sh` at the
root of the repository and open `_site/r/index.html`. It has a
getting-started vignette and articles on travel-time matrices,
accessibility, expanded and arrival matrices, detailed itineraries,
fares, elevation, scenarios, inspecting a network, how the engine works,
and benchmarks. To go from points to maps with sf, dplyr and ggplot2,
start with [“peabiru with sf and the
tidyverse”](https://strategicprojects.github.io/peabiru-routing/r/articles/sf-tidyverse.html):
an sf grid in any coordinate reference system, the routing functions
with the native pipe, dplyr on the tibbles they return, joins back to
the geometry and `geom_sf()` maps.

## Licence and credits

MIT. The routing model follows Conveyal’s R5 (MIT), from which the
routing logic is ported. The functions are modelled on those of
[r5r](https://github.com/ipea/r5r) (MIT, Ipea): the fare calculator and
parts of the trip planner are translated from its Java code, many
functions share their names, arguments and result layouts with r5r’s,
and the sample network is cut from the São Paulo sample data of the r5r
project.

The notices of the works peabiru derives from are in
`inst/LICENSE-THIRD-PARTY`. The package’s compiled code also contains
Rust crates by other authors (extendr, miniz_oxide and others): they are
listed in `inst/AUTHORS`, with their licence texts in
`inst/LICENSE-RUST-CRATES`.

# Package index

## Networks

Build a network once from a directory with an OpenStreetMap `.pbf` and
GTFS feeds.

- [`build_network()`](build_network.md) : Build a transport network

## Travel times

Travel-time matrices by street or by public transport, summarised over
the departure window or trip by trip.

- [`travel_time_matrix()`](travel_time_matrix.md) : Calculate travel
  time matrix between origin destination pairs considering a departure
  time
- [`expanded_travel_time_matrix()`](expanded_travel_time_matrix.md) :
  Calculate minute-by-minute travel times between origin destination
  pairs
- [`arrival_travel_time_matrix()`](arrival_travel_time_matrix.md) :
  Calculate travel time matrix between origin destination pairs
  considering a time of arrival

## Accessibility

- [`accessibility()`](accessibility.md) : Calculate access to
  opportunities

## Fares

Fare structures (how much each ride and transfer costs), which the
routing functions take, and the trade-off between travel time and fare.

- [`setup_fare_structure()`](setup_fare_structure.md) : Setup a fare
  structure to calculate the monetary costs of trips
- [`read_fare_structure()`](read_fare_structure.md) : Read a fare
  structure object from a file
- [`write_fare_structure()`](write_fare_structure.md) : Write a fare
  structure object to disk
- [`pareto_frontier()`](pareto_frontier.md) : Calculate travel time and
  monetary cost Pareto frontier

## Isochrones and itineraries

The areas or street segments reached from each origin within each
cutoff, and the legs of each trip.

- [`isochrone()`](isochrone.md) : Estimate isochrones from a given
  location
- [`detailed_itineraries()`](detailed_itineraries.md) : Detailed
  itineraries between origin-destination pairs

## Trip options

A multi-criteria trip planner: every trip worth considering on time,
fare, transfers and walking.

- [`trip_options()`](trip_options.md) : Trip options between
  origin-destination pairs

## Facility location

Where to open new facilities (maximal covering, set covering, p-median,
p-center), and supply against demand around each place (two-step
floating catchment area).

- [`locate_facilities()`](locate_facilities.md) : Choose where to open
  new facilities
- [`floating_catchment()`](floating_catchment.md) : Supply against
  demand around each place: the two-step floating catchment area

## Inspecting a network

Where points snap, the street and transit networks as `sf`, the dates
with service, and the errors gtfs-lib finds in the feeds.

- [`find_snap()`](find_snap.md) : Find snapped locations of input points
  on street network
- [`street_network_bbox()`](street_network_bbox.md) : Extract the
  geographic bounding box of the transport network
- [`street_network_to_sf()`](street_network_to_sf.md) : Extract
  OpenStreetMap network in sf format
- [`transit_network_to_sf()`](transit_network_to_sf.md) : Extract
  transit network in sf format
- [`check_transit_availability()`](check_transit_availability.md) :
  Check transit service availability by date
- [`get_gtfs_errors()`](get_gtfs_errors.md) : Get GTFS errors
  encountered in network building

## The package

- [`peabiru`](peabiru-package.md)
  [`peabiru-package`](peabiru-package.md) : peabiru: multimodal routing
  on OpenStreetMap and GTFS networks
- [`core_version()`](core_version.md) : Version of the Rust routing core

# Articles

### Using peabiru

- [Get started with peabiru](peabiru.md):

- [Travel-time matrices](travel-time-matrices.md):

- [Accessibility](accessibility.md):

- [Expanded and arrival matrices](expanded-and-arrival.md):

- [Detailed itineraries](itineraries.md):

  The legs of each trip, with their times, distances, routes and
  geometries: the fastest trip, the alternatives, and the street edges a
  trip uses.

- [Fares and Pareto frontiers](fares.md):

  Fare structures, travel times within a budget, the trade-off between
  time and fare, and alternative itineraries with their fares.

- [Trip options](trip-options.md):

  peabiru’s own trip planner: every trip worth considering between two
  points, on time, fare, transfers and walking, with the legs of each.

- [Facility location](facility-location.md):

  Where to open new facilities (maximal covering, set covering,
  p-median, p-center) and supply against demand around each place
  (two-step floating catchment area), on the travel times of the
  network.

- [Elevation](elevation.md):

  Slope costs for walking and cycling from an elevation raster: the two
  cost functions, rasters in projected coordinate systems, voids, and
  results that do not depend on the machine.

- [Scenarios: car speeds and traffic stress](scenarios.md):

  Change the car speed of streets, by way or by area, and the level of
  traffic stress cyclists meet, for one routing call.

- [Inspecting a network](network-inspection.md):

  Where points snap to the streets, the street and transit networks as
  sf, the dates with service, and the errors in the GTFS feeds.

- [Compared with r5r](coming-from-r5r.md):

  What peabiru shares with r5r 2.5.0, how the results of the two are
  checked to be the same, every difference between them, and how to move
  a script from one to the other.

### Examples

- [peabiru with sf and the tidyverse](sf-tidyverse.md):

  From points to maps with the tools you already use: an sf grid,
  routing with the native pipe, dplyr on the tibbles peabiru returns,
  joins back to the geometry and ggplot2’s geom_sf().

- [Example: isochrones by mode](isochrones.md):

  Areas reached from one point in Porto Alegre within 10, 20 and 30
  minutes, walking, cycling, driving and by public transport.

- [Example: mapping access to jobs and schools](accessibility-map.md):

  Travel times from one point to a grid, and the jobs and schools
  reachable within 30 minutes from every cell of Porto Alegre, walking
  and by public transport.

- [Example: how much a trip by public transport varies](trips.md):

  Percentiles of the travel time on a frequency-based network, and one
  trip split into walking, waiting and riding, departure by departure.

- [Example: the Recife metropolitan region by public
  transport](recife-metropolitan.md):

  The 14 municipalities of the Recife metropolitan region as one
  network, with the buses, the metro and the VLT of the GTFS feed of
  Grande Recife: isochrones by mode, access to schools and health units
  on a grid of the Censo 2022, what the rail lines add, how much a trip
  varies with the minute one leaves, and the options of one trip.

- [Example: access to schools and health care in Recife and
  Caruaru](recife-caruaru.md):

  From open data to accessibility for two cities of Pernambuco: an
  OpenStreetMap extract cut with osmium, the population of the Censo
  2022 on a hexagonal grid, public schools from INEP and health units
  from CNES, and the walking, cycling and driving times to the nearest
  of each.

- [Example: terrain, in Pernambuco and in Salvador](terrain.md):

  What an elevation raster changes in walking and cycling times: the
  Recife metropolitan region as one network, six municipalities of
  Pernambuco from the coast to the Sertão, and Salvador, in Bahia, as
  the steepest case, with the Copernicus elevation model checked against
  the ground first: at 30 m it reads the roofs, and a flat district
  shows how much that costs.

- [Example: who reaches the jobs in São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro and Belo
  Horizonte](capitals.md):

  Access to jobs, schools and health facilities by public transport in
  three Brazilian capitals with an official, open GTFS feed, by income,
  on the grid of Ipea’s Access to Opportunities Project; and, in Porto
  Alegre, what a fare budget leaves of that access.

- [Example: before and after in Porto
  Alegre](scenarios-porto-alegre.md):

  What-if questions answered without rebuilding the network: a new cycle
  path, congestion and a closed avenue, one more health facility, and a
  change in the fare rules, each with its map and its timing.

- [Example: jobs by public transport in Helsinki](helsinki.md):

  A city outside Brazil, from open data: the streets of the Helsinki
  capital region from OpenStreetMap, HSL’s timetables, and HSY’s 250 m
  grids of residents and jobs; access to jobs at the morning peak,
  isochrones from the Central Station, and the options for one trip.
